question: What services does BPI offer?
html:
BPI is a political, public affairs and reputation communications firm. We run campaign and advocacy work, public affairs and PR for corporate and issue clients, and paid media placement for those programs. We work from 14 offices in six countries, and London is our second-largest hub (BPI public filings; BPI growth plan).

What we do today

  • Political and campaign work. Federal committees paid BPI $115.3M in the 2024 cycle. Most of that is pass-through media spend, not BPI fee revenue (BPI public filings).
  • Advocacy. We serve non-federal political, issue-advocacy and corporate advocacy clients. Federal election filings do not capture this work (BPI public filings).
  • Public affairs and PR. Our revenue is benchmarked to public-affairs and PR norms of roughly $240-340K net revenue per person (est.). We are building this into a reputation offer for the AI era (BPI public filings; BPI growth plan).
  • Europe. We added UK firms in October 2024, and Germany is our third-largest market (BPI public filings; BPI growth plan).

What we are building

The growth plan expands the offer in phases (BPI growth plan).

PhaseOfferStatus
OneSignalOS: narrative monitoring, synthetic message testing and outcome dashboards, sold as always-on retainersPlanned launch; KPI roadmap assumes retainers live by October 2027 (est.)
TwoNamed practices in AI and tech policy, energy and critical minerals, health (Boston), and litigation and oversightPlanned
TwoFederal capture team for about $250M of tracked agency communications recompetesPlanned; no prime awards today

SignalOS will be introduced first through the 2026 Reputation Resilience Index briefings. In that research, 81% of adults say AI makes false rumors too easy to spread (BPI growth plan).

What we cannot yet say

  • We have no service-line revenue split. Management accounts by practice would show how fee revenue divides between political, advocacy, public affairs and media work.
  • We have no breakdown of what each add-on contributes. These include BOLDT, Agado and 365 Sherpas. A capabilities and client list for each firm would fill this gap.

Moving the mix from election-driven projects toward recurring retainers is the central value lever. Political billings swung from $3.1M in 2022 to $115.3M in 2024. The growth plan's exit case assumes about 55% recurring revenue by October 2029 (est.).

Next actions

  1. Get a fee-revenue split by service line and client type for 2024 and 2025 from management.
  2. Map each add-on's capabilities and clients onto the four planned practices.
  3. Set a launch date and pricing for SignalOS retainers tied to the Reputation Resilience Index briefings.
  4. Confirm a current, public-facing description of services by office, especially London and Germany.
